# V1.7.1 — running ledger of code changes

**Charter (set 2026-07-25):** the active running batch — successor to [v1.7.0.md](v1.7.0.md) (released to closed testing 2026-07-24, all items complete). Same rule as every version doc — the running catch-all for every code change we accumulate, big or small, until it is built and committed. Any tweak, fix, copy change, or feature we decide on gets booked here as a numbered item first, so nothing slips between conversations.

**Origin of this batch:** Alvin opened Settings → Notifications and found only a single row (the v1.6.6 Item 7 "Budget alerts" toggle — by design, since the planned "couple activity" toggle was dropped when it turned out to gate nothing real). Wants to populate the submodule with real personalization. Items 2-4 are **booked for grilling, not yet designed to build-ready** — this doc only records the ask + the open design tensions each one raises. **Item 1 is GRILLED + design-locked 2026-07-25 ([ADR-0052](../adr/0052-recurring-due-date-reminder-foreground.md)) — ready to build (Sonnet, medium).** Item 5 is an unrelated bug fix, no grill needed.

**Note on Items 2/3/4:** all three modify the same subsystem — [CheckBudgetAlertsUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/budgets/domain/usecase/CheckBudgetAlertsUseCase.kt) (currently hardcoded `THRESHOLDS = listOf(80, 100)`), [BudgetAlertWorker](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/budgets/worker/BudgetAlertWorker.kt), and the [NotificationsScreen](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/settings/presentation/NotificationsScreen.kt) prefs. **GRILLED TOGETHER + design-locked 2026-07-25 ([ADR-0054](../adr/0054-configurable-budget-alert-thresholds.md)) — ready to build, Sonnet/medium.** The grill collapsed the design to **zero schema/Room/Supabase change** (the synced `budgets` column the Item-4 booking predicted was rejected — the mute is a local per-device preference). Key outcomes: **one** master switch (the existing Budgets category switch from Item 6, reused — no second on/off); a **three-rung model** (warn 5–100% default 80% · limit fixed 100% · over 110–300% default 120%, own opt-in toggle default OFF); alerts deduped by **slot name** (`warn`/`limit`/`over`) not numeric threshold, which **amends [ADR-0053](../adr/0053-notification-inbox-synced-source-of-truth.md)'s inbox id** (`{threshold}` → `{slot}`) and makes per-device thresholds duplicate-safe; warn collapses into limit at 100%; per-budget mute lives in each Budgets-row ⋮ menu (🔕 marker), local + per-category so it persists across months and is per-device on shared budgets. **Build order fixed: Item 6 → this slice** (the slot-name id must be built inside Item 6). Item 1 is architecturally unrelated and was grilled separately (2026-07-25, [ADR-0052](../adr/0052-recurring-due-date-reminder-foreground.md)) — the "new scheduled-notification infra" it was expected to need was **declined** in favor of riding the existing foreground `BudgetAlertWorker` pattern.

**Decision (Alvin, 2026-07-25): the Notifications screen is becoming sectioned, not a flat list.** Since more notification types are expected over time (starting with Item 1's recurring due-date reminder), Items 2, 3, and 4 — the master on/off, the warning-threshold slider, the over-budget slider, and the per-budget mute — all live together under a **"Budgets" section** header on the Notifications screen. Item 1 (recurring reminders) is a *different* notification category and does not belong in that section. **Resolved at Item 1's grill (2026-07-25):** Item 1 ships as **one flat row, no sectioning** — sectioning is only warranted at 4+ controls, so the Items 2-4 slice owns the `NotificationsScreen`/`NotificationsUiState` sectioned-list refactor (and its exact grouping/labels), not Item 1.

**Idea considered and dropped (Alvin, 2026-07-25): a blanket "notify me when my partner logs a transaction" (excluding transfers/transfer fees).** Discussed at length: technically it would have been cheap to build (the same post-sync diff pattern `BudgetAlertWorker` already uses, hooking into `MainActivity.kt`'s post-`sync()` call and `SyncWorker`'s post-sync cycle — no new scheduling infra needed, unlike Item 1). Dropped anyway for two reasons: **(1) frequency** — a couple's day-to-day spending could mean several notifications a day, a completely different bloat category from budget alerts or a once-per-cycle due-date reminder; **(2) it cuts against the app's own existing restraint** — the app deliberately never shows partner balances and deliberately offers a Private flag so a user can keep specific transactions from their partner (ADR-0004/0005/0011); a live "your partner just spent ₱X" push runs counter to that design philosophy. Also, since sync is foreground/reconnect/pull-to-refresh only (ADR-0012), it wouldn't even be timely — it'd surface hours late at the next sync, with the annoyance of a push but none of the immediacy that would justify it. **Not booked.** Revisit only with a fresh concrete need (matching the CSV-export precedent — that stayed shelved until a tester surfaced a real use case).

**Items 6-9 added 2026-07-25** — grew out of deciding *where* Items 1-4 (and the dropped partner-transaction idea above) would actually surface. The app has no persistent notification bell/inbox today (the only real notification infra is `BudgetAlertNotifier`'s ephemeral OS system-tray push); Item 6 books that facility. Items 7-8 are an unrelated IA cleanup (relocating Export and Recurring) that surfaced in the same placement discussion but doesn't depend on the bell. Item 9 is the one couple-notification idea that survived the drop above (partner logs a **new debt** only — not a payment, not a general transaction).

## Item 1 — Recurring due-date reminder notification (un-deferred from [deferred.md Item 40](deferred.md#item-40--payday--bill-due-date-reminder-notification-needs-grill))

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `a48ef17`** 2026-07-27 (Sonnet/medium) — built, `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` (1186) green, on-device verified. Grilled + design-locked 2026-07-25 ([ADR-0052](../adr/0052-recurring-due-date-reminder-foreground.md)). **Model: Sonnet, medium effort** — the grill collapsed this from the anticipated Opus-level background-scheduling problem into a **pattern-follow**: it mirrors the existing `BudgetAlertWorker` reactive-notification flow and reuses `ObservePendingConfirmationsUseCase` wholesale. No new architectural risk (the ADR-0012 tension was resolved *by declining* the risky path). No schema/Room change.
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-25):** a reminder notification for a recurring rule, income or expense — **no advance warning**, just a due-date nudge. Draft copy (kept as-is):
  - Income: *"Did your [category] arrive? Confirm it now to record!"*
  - Expense: *"Have you paid for your [category]? Confirm it now to record!"*
- **Why now:** re-surfaces [deferred.md Item 40](deferred.md#item-40--payday--bill-due-date-reminder-notification-needs-grill) (originally split out of [v1.6.6.md Item 37](v1.6.6.md#item-37--confirm-on-arrival-recurring--incomebill-forecasting)'s Q14, deferred 2026-07-17 as "unnecessary for now"). Common, expected feature; gives the Notifications submodule a second real row.

### Grill outcome (2026-07-25) — full design resolved, [ADR-0052](../adr/0052-recurring-due-date-reminder-foreground.md)

**The central ADR-0012 tension was resolved by choosing the cheap, compliant path and explicitly declining the heavy one.** The grill first went down the real-OS-alarm branch (`AlarmManager` while-idle, boot-reschedule, exact-alarm Play-policy caution on targetSdk 36), then Alvin reconsidered: the only thing a scheduled alarm buys over the existing passive "To confirm" card is *off-app reach* — and on his own Transsion/MTK device (force-stops the app above Doze), a force-stopped app gets **no alarms and no workers** until reopened, so the heavy path buys a guarantee that's weakest exactly where it matters. Decision: **ride the foreground reactive-notification pattern instead.**

| Decision | Resolution |
|---|---|
| **Reach / mechanism** | **App-open / sync-triggered**, *not* a clock alarm. New `RecurringReminderWorker` mirrors `BudgetAlertWorker`, enqueued at the same two sites ([MainActivity.kt:248](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/MainActivity.kt#L248) post-sync, [SyncWorker.kt:47](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/sync/SyncWorker.kt#L47) post-sync). No `AlarmManager`, no `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED`. ADR-0012-clean. |
| **Rule scope** | **Confirm-on-arrival only** (`auto_post=false`). Auto-post rules record silently — nothing to confirm, copy doesn't apply. Reuses [ObservePendingConfirmationsUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/recurring/domain/usecase/ObservePendingConfirmationsUseCase.kt) wholesale (its ~3-month floor window + paused-rule + already-materialized filtering all come for free). |
| **Timing** | **Catch-up, fire once per occurrence.** Fires the first time the app opens *on or after* the due date for a still-pending occurrence — never before (no advance warning). Not strict same-day (which, on an app-open trigger, would fire almost never). One nudge per occurrence via a local `RecurringReminderStore` keyed on `occurrenceId` (mirrors `BudgetAlertStore`). |
| **Backlog guard** | On first enable, seed all currently-pending occurrences into the store as already-notified *without firing* — same trick `BudgetAlertWorker` uses — so shipping this (default ON) doesn't dump the backlog; only new occurrences fire going forward. |
| **Suppression** | Paused rules (`is_paused`) and already-confirmed occurrences suppressed **automatically** — falls out of reusing the pending list, not new code. |
| **Toggle** | **One combined** "Recurring reminders" DataStore boolean (new key alongside `budget_alerts_enabled`), **default ON** (matches `budgetAlertsEnabled`). Copy branches income/expense internally; not split into two switches. |
| **Screen** | **Add one flat row** to [NotificationsScreen](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/settings/presentation/NotificationsScreen.kt) now. Sectioning is **deferred to Items 2-4** (sectioning is only warranted at 4+ controls, and its labels are that grill's call). |
| **Volume** | **One notification per occurrence, bundled under an Android `setGroup` key** — keeps the personalized per-category copy while collapsing a payday cluster (salary + several bills same day) into one tray stack. Dedicated "Recurring reminders" notification channel, distinct from "Budget Alerts". |
| **Tap** | **Deep-link to the confirm surface** — the Records "To confirm" card (or the Recurring module once [Item 8](#item-8--promote-recurring-to-its-own-top-level-module) lands), reusing the balance widget's `pendingWidgetRoute` deep-link plumbing. |
| **Couples / schema** | Fully personal (recurring rules are owner-only; reminders per-device). **No couples-governance question, no synced column, no Room migration**, ADR-0009 order unaffected. |

**Build shape (sibling-worker pattern, copy from `BudgetAlertWorker`):** new `RecurringReminderWorker` + `RecurringReminderNotifier` (its own channel) + `RecurringReminderStore` (DataStore/prefs, `occurrenceId`→notified) + a `CheckRecurringDueUseCase` that diffs `ObservePendingConfirmationsUseCase`'s current output against the store; wire the worker into the two existing enqueue sites; add the "Recurring reminders" toggle (repo key + Observe/Set use cases mirroring `budgetAlertsEnabled`) and one row on the Notifications screen; add the deep-link route. **Tier-1 tests:** the diff/fire-once + first-enable-seed logic in `CheckRecurringDueUseCase` (pure Kotlin — the store-diff and backlog-seed are the bug-prone parts).

**Note:** the plan above predates [Item 6 / ADR-0053](#item-6--notification-bell--in-app-inbox-facility), landed 2026-07-27, which retired the standalone-notifier-plus-store shape in favor of the shared inbox — see Build outcome below for what was actually built.

### Build outcome (2026-07-27) — `a48ef17`

**Files touched:** new `CheckRecurringDueUseCase` + `RecurringReminderCopy` (pure Kotlin, `feature/recurring/domain/usecase/`), `RecurringReminderBacklogStore` (`feature/recurring/data/`), `RecurringReminderWorker` (`feature/recurring/worker/`, sibling to `BudgetAlertWorker`), `CheckRecurringDueUseCaseTest` (7 tests); `NotificationPreferencesRepository`/`Impl` (+`recurringRemindersEnabled`), `ObserveRecurringRemindersEnabledUseCase`/`SetRecurringRemindersEnabledUseCase`, `NotificationsUiState`/`ViewModel`/`Screen` (new "Recurring reminders" row); `MainActivity.kt` (new `ROUTE_RECORDS` deep-link constant + worker enqueue), `SyncWorker.kt` (worker enqueue). New `supabase/seeds/recurring_reminder_scenario.sql` for on-device verification (mirrors `budget_alert_scenario.sql`).

**As-built vs. the grilled plan (ADR-0053 consequence, expected):** no standalone `RecurringReminderNotifier`/per-occurrence `RecurringReminderStore` — the worker writes an inbox row via `RecordNotificationUseCase` (create-if-absent is the dedup, `recurring:{occurrenceId}` id) and only a genuinely-new row raises the push through `SystemNotificationPresenter`, exactly like `BudgetAlertWorker`. `RecurringReminderBacklogStore` survives as a much narrower piece: a one-time local freeze of whatever was pending on the device's first-ever run, so shipping (default ON) doesn't dump a 3-month backlog of reminders at once (ADR-0052 decision 3) — the inbox itself isn't enough for that guarantee since it has no concept of "existed before this feature could fire."

**Bug found + fixed during on-device verification:** the backlog store freezes *raw* occurrence ids, but the worker merged them into the inbox's `alreadyRaisedIds` set (which holds `recurring:`-prefixed ids) without re-prefixing — a silent no-op that would have let the very first pending occurrence fire on a fresh install instead of being suppressed. Caught by seeding an already-due rule on the server *before* the very first app sync (exactly the backlog scenario), invisible to the unit tests since they exercise `CheckRecurringDueUseCase` directly with correctly-shaped ids. Fixed by mapping the backlog through `CheckRecurringDueUseCase.notificationId()` before merging.

**On-device verification (emulator, Medium_Phone AVD, staging seed via Supabase MCP):** confirmed on a fresh install (`pm clear`) — a rule already due before first-ever sync is correctly suppressed (no row, no push); a rule added after the backlog freeze fires correctly, INCOME and EXPENSE copy both correct ("Did your [category] arrive?" / "Have you paid for your [category]?"); inbox row renders with the recurring icon and no dark-mode contrast issues; tap deep-links to Records' "To confirm" card; no duplicate fire on a second sync of the same occurrence; Settings → Notifications toggle renders and defaults ON. Seeded staging data cleaned up after.

## Item 2 — Configurable warning threshold (replaces the hardcoded 80%)

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `aff2166`** 2026-07-27 (Sonnet/medium) — built + on-device verified together with Items 3-4 (grilled and built as one subsystem slice, [ADR-0054](../adr/0054-configurable-budget-alert-thresholds.md)). See [Build outcome](#build-outcome-items-2-4-2026-07-27--aff2166) below.
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-25):** "I need a slider so the user can manually choose which threshold they want their budgets to fire notification, it is a one slider for all... the slider stepper would be 5%. From 5% to 100%, going over 100% triggers a different message." **Intent: personalization.**
- **What this replaces:** [CheckBudgetAlertsUseCase.THRESHOLDS](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/budgets/domain/usecase/CheckBudgetAlertsUseCase.kt#L53)'s hardcoded `listOf(80, 100)`. This item owns the **warn** rung: a single user-chosen value, applies to all budgets, **5–100% in 5% steps, default 80%** (matches today, so existing users see no change). Warn fires only strictly *below* 100% — at exactly 100% it collapses into the fixed `limit` rung (decision 4).
- **Master switch (resolved):** **one** switch, not two — the existing "Budget alerts" toggle (`budgetAlertsEnabled`, v1.6.6 Item 7), which Item 6/[ADR-0053](../adr/0053-notification-inbox-synced-source-of-truth.md) repurposes as the **Budgets category switch**. Item 2 adds only the slider beneath it; there is no second on/off. Off ⇒ nothing budget-related fires; per-budget mute state (Item 4) is preserved untouched.
- **Storage:** new **local** DataStore Int in `NotificationPreferencesRepository` (mirrors `budgetAlertsEnabled`) — per-device, not synced (decision 5). Cross-device duplication is prevented by the slot-name dedup (Item 3 / decision 3), not by syncing settings.
- **Full design:** [ADR-0054](../adr/0054-configurable-budget-alert-thresholds.md).

## Item 3 — Over-budget "way over" threshold slider (110%–300%, own on/off toggle)

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `aff2166`** 2026-07-27 (Sonnet/medium) — built + on-device verified together with Items 2+4. See [Build outcome](#build-outcome-items-2-4-2026-07-27--aff2166) below.
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-25):** a second slider notification, independently toggleable on/off, for when spend crosses past 100%. **Intent: personalization — let the user know their budget has been badly exceeded.**
- **Resolved design:** the `over` rung — **a single trip-wire**, not repeated nagging: one "way over budget" alert fires when spend crosses the chosen value, and that's it for the month. **110–300% in 10% steps, default 120%, its own on/off toggle default OFF** (a new alert type, opt-in). 300% is simply the slider max (Reading A, decision 2/3) — not a "stop nagging past 300%" ceiling.
- **The 100%–110% "gap" is a non-issue:** the fixed `limit` rung always fires at exactly 100% (decision 2), so there is never a silent zone between the limit alert and the user's chosen `over` value.
- **Dedup (decision 3):** deduped by **slot name** `over` (not the numeric value), so moving the slider mid-month never re-fires an already-fired `over`, and two devices at different `over` values still map to one inbox row. This is the change that **amends [ADR-0053](../adr/0053-notification-inbox-synced-source-of-truth.md)'s id** from `{threshold}` to `{slot}` — build it that way inside Item 6.
- **Copy:** title `[Category] way over budget`, body `You've spent [X]% of your [Category] budget.`
- **Full design:** [ADR-0054](../adr/0054-configurable-budget-alert-thresholds.md).

## Item 4 — Per-budget mute toggle (Budgets submodule)

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `aff2166`** 2026-07-27 (Sonnet/medium) — built + on-device verified together with Items 2-3. See [Build outcome](#build-outcome-items-2-4-2026-07-27--aff2166) below.
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-25):** "I also want in the Budgets submodule to have a button to turn on/off notification for each budget entry. I didn't want a slider for each budget as it bloats things up, but at least a turn on/off button would suffice per budget entry." **Intent: personalization** — a coarse per-row mute sitting underneath the two global sliders.
- **Schema impact: NONE (this reversed at grill).** The synced `budgets.notificationsEnabled` column the booking predicted was **rejected**: (a) it would contradict the local/per-device posture of every other notification pref, (b) it would sync the mute to the partner on shared budgets (unwanted), and (c) budgets are **per-month rows**, so a column would reset the mute every month. Instead the mute is a **local DataStore set** keyed per budget *line* (category/scope), so it **persists across months** and is per-device. **No Room migration, no Supabase column, no DTO/mapper change.**
- **Shared budgets (resolved):** per-device — muting a shared budget silences only *your* alerts; the partner keeps theirs unless they mute on their own device (falls out of local storage; consistent with ADR-0004/0005/0011).
- **UI placement (resolved):** the mute toggles ("Mute alerts" / "Unmute alerts") live in each budget row's **existing ⋮ overflow menu** in [BudgetsScreen](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/budgets/presentation/BudgetsScreen.kt) (alongside Reset rollover / Duplicate / Delete), plus a 🔕 marker on muted rows — no always-visible per-row switch (the row is already dense; muting is rare).
- **Precedence (resolved):** mute = **total silence** for that one budget — all three rungs (warn/limit/over), both inbox row and OS push. It only ever *narrows* what the master switch allows, never widens it. When the master Budgets switch is off, per-budget mute state is preserved untouched (turning the master back on resumes each budget exactly as set).
- **Full design:** [ADR-0054](../adr/0054-configurable-budget-alert-thresholds.md).

### Build outcome (Items 2-4, 2026-07-27) — `aff2166`

**Files touched:** `CheckBudgetAlertsUseCase.kt` (new `rungs(warnPercent, overPercent)` factory — warn collapses into limit at exactly 100%, `over` omitted entirely when its toggle is off); `BudgetAlertWorker.kt` (reads the new prefs, excludes muted budget lines before checking, builds rungs dynamically, syncs the over-rung backlog each run); new `BudgetOverAlertBacklogStore.kt` (local DataStore snapshot of currently-over budgets while the `over` toggle is off — the "seed the over slot as fired while off" build-time recommendation from the ADR's Consequences section, implemented so enabling the toggle later doesn't blast pre-existing crossings); new `BudgetLineId.kt` (stable `personal:{categoryId}` / `shared:{categoryId}` key for the mute, independent of the per-month `Budget.id`); `NotificationPreferencesRepository`/`Impl` (+3 local DataStore keys, +1 muted-lines string set) and 8 new settings usecases; `NotificationsScreen`/`UiState`/`ViewModel` (new sectioned "Budgets" header: master switch → warn slider → over toggle → over slider, greying out — not hiding — when the master is off; "Recurring reminders" stays its own flat row below, per Item 1's own grill); `BudgetsUiState`/`ViewModel`/`Screen` (`BudgetRow.isMuted`, `toggleMute()`, "Mute alerts"/"Unmute alerts" in the row's ⋮ menu, 🔕 marker). No schema/Room/Supabase change, as the ADR predicted.

**Tests added:** 7 new cases in `CheckBudgetAlertsUseCaseTest` covering the `rungs()` factory — user-chosen warn percent, warn-collapse-at-exactly-100, over omitted when its toggle is off, over fires at/above the chosen threshold and not below, and a slider-move-mid-month doesn't re-fire an already-raised rung. Suite at 20/20 for this file; full `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green throughout.

**Bug found + fixed during on-device verification:** the threshold sliders didn't snap to their declared step size — Compose `Slider`'s `steps` param only snaps the *rendered thumb*, not the raw value delivered to `onValueChange`, so a tap could land off-grid (e.g. "39%" instead of "40%"). Fixed by snapping explicitly in the callback (`NotificationsScreen.kt`).

**On-device verification (emulator, staging flavor, seeded via Supabase MCP):** Budgets section layout correct (master switch → warn slider → over toggle → over slider, Recurring reminders unsectioned below); master-off greys out both sliders without hiding them; lowering the warn slider below current spend fires correctly; enabling the over toggle after a budget was already past threshold does **not** blast a notification for the pre-existing crossing (backlog-seed working as designed), while a genuinely new crossing after enabling does fire; per-budget mute silences all three rungs for that budget while a control budget fires normally, and unmuting resumes it; mute-key persistence across months confirmed by code inspection (`BudgetLineId` keys on category+scope, never the per-month row id). All seeded test data cleaned from staging afterward.

## Item 5 — Manage-module kebab (⋮ overflow) icons stay black in dark mode

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `ec72e41`** 2026-07-28 (Sonnet/low) — built + on-device verified. **Model: Sonnet, low effort** — mechanical one-line-per-file fix matching an already-correct pattern used everywhere else in the codebase; no grill needed. No schema/Room change.
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-25):** the kebab (three-dot overflow) buttons somewhere in the Manage module — Alvin wasn't sure exactly which submodule, guessed Accounts, Budgets, or Categories — stay black even in dark mode.
- **Root cause (confirmed by inspection, not yet fixed):** every screen's row-level `Icon(Icons.Filled.MoreVert, ...)` is supposed to pass an explicit `tint = colors.textSecondary` (`colors` = [LocalPlayfulColors](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/ui/theme/) — the app's custom Playful theme, which is what actually drives dark-mode color, not the default M3 `LocalContentColor`). [TransactionsScreen.kt:184-188](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsScreen.kt#L184-L188) (×2 instances), [RecurringScreen.kt:464-467](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/recurring/presentation/RecurringScreen.kt#L464-L467), [NotesScreen.kt:250-253](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/notes/presentation/NotesScreen.kt#L250-L253), and [GoalDetailScreen.kt:340](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/savings/presentation/GoalDetailScreen.kt#L340) all do this correctly. Exactly **three call sites never got the `tint` param** and fall back to the M3 default, which doesn't flip with the app's dark mode — all three are the Manage module's per-row overflow menus Alvin was describing:
  - [AccountsScreen.kt:456](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/accounts/presentation/AccountsScreen.kt#L456)
  - [BudgetsScreen.kt:224](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/budgets/presentation/BudgetsScreen.kt#L224)
  - [CategoriesScreen.kt:473](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/categories/presentation/CategoriesScreen.kt#L473)
  - **Also found in the same sweep, same bug, not reported by Alvin but worth fixing together (one-line, same root cause):** [GoalDetailScreen.kt:114](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/savings/presentation/GoalDetailScreen.kt#L114) (the goal-detail screen's *other* kebab — the header one at line 114 is missing `tint`, while its contribution-row one at line 340 already has it).
- **Change:** add `tint = colors.textSecondary` to each of the 4 call sites above, matching the already-correct sibling instances verbatim. Pure Compose, no new state, no logic change.
- **Verify:** `assembleStagingDebug` green (pure visual, no tier-1 tests — matches the no-test precedent for static Composable tweaks). On-device: switch to dark mode, open Manage → Accounts / Budgets / Categories and Savings → a goal's detail, confirm all kebab icons render themed (matching the rest of each screen's icon/text color) instead of black.

### Build outcome (2026-07-28) — `ec72e41`

**Files touched:** `AccountsScreen.kt`, `BudgetsScreen.kt`, `CategoriesScreen.kt` (each row-level overflow `Icon()` gained `tint = colors.textSecondary`); `GoalDetailScreen.kt` (the header kebab gained the tint — `colors` wasn't in scope in that composable yet, so `val colors = LocalPlayfulColors.current` was added at the top of `GoalDetailScreen`). `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` (unchanged suite) green — no tier-1 tests needed, pure Compose tint fix with no logic change.

**On-device verification (emulator, Medium_Phone AVD, dark mode):** Accounts/Budgets/Categories row kebabs all render themed instead of black; the goal-detail header kebab (newly fixed) matches the tint of the already-correct contribution-row kebab. Verified against a throwaway "Kebab" savings goal created for the check (no goals existed on the test account), deleted afterward. Light-mode spot-check on Categories showed no regression. No bugs found.

## Item 6 — Notification bell / in-app inbox facility

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `ccf933b`** 2026-07-27 (Opus/high) — built, `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` (1179) green, on-device verified. Grilled + design-locked 2026-07-25 ([ADR-0053](../adr/0053-notification-inbox-synced-source-of-truth.md)). **Model: Opus, high effort** — new *synced* domain entity, a cross-cutting per-screen bell rollout, and it becomes the shared delivery layer every other notification type in this doc (Items 1, 2-4, 9) routes through. **Room v30** + Supabase migration #22. **Sequencing: Item 6 landed *before* Item 1** — Item 1's [ADR-0052](../adr/0052-recurring-due-date-reminder-foreground.md) is amended by consequence to write an inbox row instead of a standalone notifier.
- **Request:** surfaced while deciding *where* Items 1-4's alerts (and the dropped partner-transaction idea above) should actually show up. The app has **no persistent notification bell or in-app inbox today** — the only real notification infra is `BudgetAlertNotifier`, the sole caller of `NotificationCompat`/`NotificationManager` anywhere in the app; there's no icon, badge, or browsable history of past notifications anywhere in the UI. Alvin wants a real bell + unread badge + tap-through history, both as a home base for the growing Notifications submodule and as a lower-cost surface than an OS push (you check it on your own schedule instead of being interrupted).

### Grill outcome (2026-07-25) — full design resolved, [ADR-0053](../adr/0053-notification-inbox-synced-source-of-truth.md)

**Term lock:** this is the **Notification inbox**; its UI affordance is the **inbox bell**. "Bell" alone stays reserved for the existing *unpair broadcast bell* (the Realtime unpair signal) — do not conflate. Glossary updated in `CONTEXT.md` → Notifications.

**The pivotal decision was "synced now, not local."** The grill first leaned local-only (per-device, no cloud table) — then Alvin flagged the web app is imminent (possibly starting the following week), which turns cross-device read state from a tablet edge-case into a real laptop+phone concern. Decision: build it **synced now**, same posture the paywall used (build infra when the consumer is actually coming).

| Decision | Resolution |
|---|---|
| **Delivery model** | **Way A — inbox-primary.** Every source writes an inbox row first (the guaranteed home); the OS tray push is a best-effort courtesy on top. Chosen over push-primary because ADR-0012 foreground-only sync + the Transsion force-stop make off-app push unreliable — the bell catches what the OS drops. |
| **Storage** | **Synced cloud table** (new Room table → **Room v30** + Supabase migration), own-user-only (RLS own-row, **no partner variant**, never replicated). A leaf depending only on the users row → sits at the **end** of the ADR-0009 push/pull order. Item 9's partner-debt notification lands in the *recipient's own* inbox as their own row. |
| **Identity** | **Deterministic per-category id** as PK (`budget:{id}:{month}:{slot}` — **amended from `{threshold}` by [ADR-0054](../adr/0054-configurable-budget-alert-thresholds.md); build the budget id with `slot ∈ {warn,limit,over}`, not the numeric threshold** — plus `recurring:{occurrenceId}`, `debt:{debtId}`) so phone + web producing the same event **merge**, not duplicate. Generation = **create-if-absent** — re-detecting an event never overwrites read/dismissed state. The inbox row's existence *becomes* the dedup record, **retiring `BudgetAlertStore`**. |
| **Retention** | **60-day window**, by *genuine deletion* not tombstone — safe because "older than 60 days" is computed identically on every client (resurrection-safe, same spirit as the month-rollover budget-alert clear). Narrow sanctioned exception to ADR-0010. User dismiss/clear-all, by contrast, is an ordinary soft-delete that syncs. |
| **Inbox surface** | **A full screen**, opened only by the bell, back-arrow to return. Not a panel, not a pinnable More-grid module. |
| **Bell placement** | **Every top-level screen's title bar**, top-right beside the privacy eye, in one rollout pass (the bell is account-global, unlike the money-only eye). Unread badge rides on the bell icon. Layout care needed on Analysis (already has Net assets + eye). |
| **Read model** | Badge = unread count. **Opening the inbox bulk-clears it** (marks all read); unread items stay highlighted *for that visit*. |
| **Manual control** | **Swipe-to-dismiss individual + Clear all** (dismiss = ordinary soft-delete, syncs). |
| **List layout** | **Flat, newest-first**, per-row category icon, light date dividers. |
| **Category toggles** | **One switch per category** in Settings → Notifications (Budgets / Recurring / Couple). Off = category silent everywhere (no bell row, no push). (Rejected: a two-level collect-in-bell / also-push split per category — real but doubles every row for a nuance few touch; addable later.) |
| **Tap target** | **Specific-with-fallback** — jump to the exact budget/debt/To-confirm card if it still exists, else its parent screen (never a dead end). Requires lightly extending the current module-root-only deep-link plumbing. |
| **Scope / sequencing** | Ships with **budget alerts migrated in** as the pilot source (proves Way A end-to-end). **Item 6 before Item 1**; Item 1's ADR-0052 amended to write an inbox row (net simplification). Items 2-4 and 9 wire into the same inbox as built. |

**Rejected alternatives (in [ADR-0053](../adr/0053-notification-inbox-synced-source-of-truth.md)):** push-primary/inbox-mirror (an OS-dropped push would leave no row — the exact failure this fixes); local-only per-device (would force a rewrite once the web app lands); fully server-generated (the "correct" long-term multi-client design, deferred to the web-app build — deterministic client ids give most of its dedup benefit without the backend).

**Downstream consequences (flagged, not re-grilled):** (1) **Item 1 re-sequenced after Item 6**, ADR-0052 amended to write an inbox row rather than a standalone `RecurringReminderNotifier`. (2) **Item 9's grill inherits a pre-answered delivery half** — it just writes a `debt:{id}` row; that grill only needs copy + settings-section placement.

### Build outcome (2026-07-27) — `ccf933b`

**Files touched (48 files, +3595/−202):** new `feature/notifications/` vertical — entity → DAO → DTO → remote source → mapper → syncer → repo → 8 use cases → DI → `InboxBell`/`NotificationInboxScreen`/`NotificationBellViewModel`/`NotificationInboxViewModel`/`SystemNotificationPresenter`; `IponDatabase` (**Room v30**, `@AutoMigration(29→30)`, `app/schemas/…/30.json`), `DatabaseModule`, `SyncTable` (`NOTIFICATIONS` last in the ADR-0009 order), `core/ui/PlayfulScreenTitle` (bell renders here, so all six top-level modules got it in one edit), `navigation/IponApp` (standalone `notification_inbox` route + `LocalInboxBell` CompositionLocal provided once at the nav shell), `IponApp.kt`; budgets pilot migration — new `BudgetAlertCopy`, rewritten `CheckBudgetAlertsUseCase`/`BudgetAlertWorker`, **deleted** `BudgetAlertStore`/`BudgetAlertModule`/`BudgetAlertNotifier`; `NotificationsScreen`/`NotificationsUiState`; `supabase/migrations/2026-07-26_notification_inbox.sql` + `supabase/schema.sql`.

**Tests added:** `NotificationMapperTest`, `NotificationRepositoryImplTest`, `NotificationTableSyncerTest`, `NotificationTestFixtures`, plus a rewritten `CheckBudgetAlertsUseCaseTest`. Suite total 1179, green.

**Supabase:** migration #22 applied + verified live on staging (11 columns, `id` is `text`, rev trigger, 2 indexes, RLS + own-row policy).

**Key build decisions (as implemented):** `record()` is atomic create-if-absent (`@Insert(IGNORE)`, returns −1) and the returned `Boolean` is the **sole** trigger for an OS push — the inbox row's existence *is* the dedup record, which is what retired `BudgetAlertStore`; month-embedded ids make rung re-arming automatic. Ids are built as `budget:{id}:{month}:{warn|limit|over}` per ADR-0054 decision 3, so **Items 2-4 only change a threshold map**. `BudgetAlertNotifier` was generalised into `SystemNotificationPresenter` (one OS channel per category; budget keeps its `budget_alerts` channel id; Recurring + Couple channels pre-registered for Items 1 and 9).

**Deviations from the grill (accepted by Alvin 2026-07-27, not re-grilled):**
1. **The "mark fired even when suppressed" seeding was dropped** per ADR-0053 decision 5. Consequence: re-enabling Budget alerts now surfaces budgets that are *actually* over, instead of pretending the crossings never happened. **ADR-0054 wants the seeding back for the opt-in `over` rung — restore it in Items 2-4.**
2. **The sectioned Notifications screen was NOT built.** ADR-0054 decision 9's parenthetical assigns it here, but ADR-0052 and ADR-0054's own consequences both put it in Items 2-4 ("only warranted at 4+ controls"); one section with one row would be worse than the current single switch. **Items 2-4 own it.**
3. **The bell is on the six `PlayfulScreenTitle` modules only — accepted as the intended scope, not an open question** (Alvin, 2026-07-27). Settings and Calculator use a plain M3 `TopAppBar` and would need a second implementation path for a bell nobody asked for on those screens. **Do not re-raise this as a loose end**; if a future notification type genuinely needs reach from Settings, that slice can reopen it on its own merits.

**On-device verification (emulator, Medium_Phone AVD):** first pass 16/17. Confirmed: bell on all six modules with no cramping, warn→limit sequence with no duplicate warn, idempotence, dismiss surviving force-stop, the Budget-alerts switch gating both surfaces, Clear all, correct slot-named ids, rows landing on staging Supabase. **Three bugs found and fixed during verification** — all three were invisible in light mode, which is worth carrying into Items 2-4:
- `SwipeToDismissBox` painted its "Dismiss" background behind *every* row permanently; `PlayfulSurface.Glass` is translucent, so read rows showed it through and rendered pinker than unread ones — inverting the highlight and leaking the label. Now drawn only mid-swipe.
- `pruneExpired` partitioned on `serverRev != null` to decide whether to issue a remote delete, but **locally-pushed rows keep `serverRev = null` in this codebase** (verified across transactions/budgets too), so every synced notification would have been hard-deleted locally with no server-side delete — orphaning rows on Supabase at the 60-day mark. Now every expired id is sent and nothing prunes locally unless that succeeds; a regression test pins it.
- `NotificationCard` hard-coded `textPrimary`/`textSecondary` (page inks) onto a Blush *card*. In dark mode `blush = lerp(primaryContainer, White, 0.85f)` is near-white, so every unread row rendered near-white on near-white; read rows masked it because Glass is a faint tint over the dark background. Now takes its ink from the existing `onPlayfulSurface(surface)` helper. **The bell itself was fine** — `InboxBell.kt` already set an explicit `tint`.

## Item 9 — Couple-section notification: partner logs a new debt

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `9453131`** 2026-07-27 (Sonnet/medium) — built, `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` (1198) green, on-device verified. Grilled + design-locked 2026-07-25. **Model: Sonnet, medium effort** — the grill collapsed this from the anticipated Opus-level "first couple-shared source" into a **pattern-follow**: delivery is fully pre-answered by [Item 6 / ADR-0053](../adr/0053-notification-inbox-synced-source-of-truth.md) (it just writes a `debt:{debtId}` inbox row), and detection is a plain synced-table cursor diff + local "seen" store that **mirrors Item 1's `RecurringReminderStore` almost exactly**. No new architectural risk. **No schema/Room change.** **Sequencing: Item 6 must land first** (the inbox + the sectioned Notifications screen are its foundation). No separate ADR — this is a thin consumer of ADR-0053.
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-25):** originally proposed alongside a "partner logs a payment" notification and a blanket "partner logs any transaction" notification (see the dropped-idea note above). After discussion, the blanket transaction idea was **dropped entirely**, and "payment logged" was **dropped**, leaving only **"partner logs a new debt."**
- **Why this one survives where the others didn't:** unlike general transactions (high-frequency, cuts against the app's existing partner-privacy restraint — ADR-0004/0005/0011) and "payment logged" (ADR-0019's auto-netting/two-leg settlement can synthesize linked `DebtPayment` rows from a single settlement action, so "a payment" isn't reliably one clean human event), a **new** `PartnerDebt` row is discrete, low-frequency (an IOU tracker isn't used daily), and unambiguous — structurally the same synced-table cursor diff as budget alerts or Item 1's recurring reminder (`PartnerDebtTableSyncer`, own `updated_at`/`server_rev`).

### Grill outcome (2026-07-25) — full design resolved

**Codebase facts that grounded the design:** new `PartnerDebt` rows come from exactly **two local paths** — manual add and "Paid for partner" (ADR-0019 #12) — and both funnel through the single `UpsertPartnerDebtUseCase` choke-point ([UpsertPartnerDebtUseCase.kt:16](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/partnerdebt/domain/usecase/UpsertPartnerDebtUseCase.kt#L16)). Auto-netting writes only `DebtPayment` rows, **never** new debts, so it's not a trigger source. There is **no `created_by` column** on `partner_debts` — the two participants are just `borrowerId`/`lenderId`, so participant identity alone can't reveal authorship.

| Decision | Resolution |
|---|---|
| **Trigger scope** | **Both origins fire** (manual + paid-for-partner). A paid-for-partner debt is *higher* signal, not lower — it means real money is owed that you may not have logged yourself. (Distinct from the dropped "partner logged a transaction" idea, which was about ambient spend visibility, not an obligation landing on you.) |
| **Direction rule (the core scope)** | Notify user U **iff** the debt was authored by the partner **AND** U is the **borrower** (U owes). "Patty logs *Alvin owes me ₱500*" → **Alvin notified**. "Patty logs *I owe Alvin*" (partner is borrower) → **silent**. "Alvin logs *Patty owes me*" → **Patty** notified, not Alvin. Every ping therefore unambiguously means *"you owe money you may not have logged yourself"* — always actionable. |
| **Detection mechanism** | Local **"authored/seen" store** (mirrors Item 1's `RecurringReminderStore`), **no schema change**. On first enable, seed all current debt ids as already-seen (backlog guard). Hook `UpsertPartnerDebtUseCase` to add each locally-authored debt id at create time → U's own debts are pre-seeded and never fire; partner debts arrive via sync only, are absent from the store, and fire. The borrower-direction check is an **additional gate** layered on top (direction alone can't tell authorship — a `borrowerId == U` row could be U's self-entered "I owe partner" or the partner's "U owes me"). Final rule: **fire for a synced debt where `borrowerId == currentUser`, the id is not in U's authored-store, and no `debt:{id}` inbox row exists yet.** (Considered + rejected: a `created_by` column — schema churn on a couples table for robustness a per-device notification doesn't need; the web app can add server-side detection later without it.) |
| **Copy** | **Content-free + amount:** *"Patty logged a new debt — you owe ₱500."* Amount shown (the actionable bit); the free-text reason/description stays **out** of the notification (it can be personal — lock-screen caution). Tap through for the reason. |
| **Delivery** | **OS push + inbox row** (not inbox-only). Timely, low-frequency → clears the interruption bar, same as budget alerts. Push may arrive slightly late given foreground-only sync (ADR-0012), but that's a *when-we-find-out* limit, not a reason to downgrade. Writes a `debt:{debtId}` inbox row via ADR-0053. |
| **Settings** | **One switch**, *"Partner debt alerts"*, **default ON**, new local DataStore boolean (mirrors `budgetAlertsEnabled`). Lives as the sole row of a new **"Couple" section** on the sectioned Notifications screen — **the section hides entirely when unpaired** (consistent with the Debt Tracker itself being paired-only). No master/sub-row hierarchy for a single item; a later grill splits it if more couple notifications arrive. |
| **Tap target** | Tap → the specific debt row in the **Partner Debt Tracker**, falling back to the Debt Tracker screen if the row is gone (ADR-0053's specific-with-fallback). |
| **Edits don't re-fire** | Only a **brand-new** debt fires; a partner editing an existing debt's amount stays silent (falls out of id-based dedup — matches the "logs a **new** debt" scope). |
| **OS channel** | Its own **"Partner debts"** notification channel, distinct from Budget Alerts / Recurring — independently OS-mutable. |
| **Private source txn** | A paid-for-partner debt still fires even if the partner marked the *source transaction* Private — the debt itself is always couple-visible (privacy flags apply to transactions, not debts). No leak. |
| **Couples/schema** | Own-user inbox row (never replicated); detection store is per-device. **No synced column, no Room migration, ADR-0009 order unaffected.** |

**Build shape (sibling-worker pattern, copy from `BudgetAlertWorker`/Item 1's `RecurringReminderWorker`):** a `SeenDebtStore` (DataStore, `debtId`→seen) + a `CheckPartnerDebtNotificationsUseCase` that diffs the synced debt list (filtered `borrowerId == currentUser`) against the store, writes a `debt:{id}` inbox row + fires the push for each unseen partner-authored debt, then marks seen; wire it into the same two post-sync enqueue sites Item 1 uses; add the "Partner debt alerts" toggle (repo key + Observe/Set use cases) and the Couple section on the Notifications screen. **Tier-1 tests:** the detection logic (borrower filter + authored-store diff + first-enable seed) — pure Kotlin, bug-prone.

### Build outcome (2026-07-27)

**Files touched:** new `CheckPartnerDebtNotificationsUseCase` + `PartnerDebtNotificationCopy` (pure Kotlin, `feature/partnerdebt/domain/usecase/`), `PartnerDebtSeenStore` (`feature/partnerdebt/data/` — combines the authored-set and the one-time backlog freeze in one store, since both feed the same "must never fire" set), `PartnerDebtNotificationWorker` (`feature/partnerdebt/worker/`, sibling to `RecurringReminderWorker`/`BudgetAlertWorker`), `CheckPartnerDebtNotificationsUseCaseTest` (6 cases); `UpsertPartnerDebtUseCase` (now calls `seenStore.markAuthored(debt.id)` at its single choke point, covering both the manual-add and paid-for-partner paths); `NotificationPreferencesRepository`/`Impl` (+`partnerDebtAlertsEnabled`, default ON), `ObservePartnerDebtAlertsEnabledUseCase`/`SetPartnerDebtAlertsEnabledUseCase`; `NotificationsUiState`/`ViewModel`/`Screen` (new "Couple" section, hidden entirely via `isPaired` — sourced from `ObserveCoupleMembersUseCase().map { it != null }`, the same pattern `AccountsViewModel`/`CategoriesViewModel` already use); `MainActivity.kt` (new `ROUTE_COUPLE` deep-link constant + worker enqueue), `SyncWorker.kt` (worker enqueue). Two existing tests (`PartnerDebtUseCaseValidationTest`, `PaidOnBehalfUseCaseTest`) updated for `UpsertPartnerDebtUseCase`'s new constructor param (a `mockk<PartnerDebtSeenStore>(relaxed = true)`). No schema/Room/Supabase change, as the grill predicted.

**Deep-link scope cut (disclosed, not a bug):** the notification opens the **Couple module root** (`ROUTE_COUPLE = "couple"`), landing on its default Combined tab — one tap from Debts — rather than the specific debt row the grill's "specific-with-fallback" language described. Jumping directly to the Debts tab or a specific row would need extending the deep-link plumbing past its current module-root-only shape (exactly what ADR-0053 flagged this item would eventually need); doing that here would have widened a thin, Sonnet/medium consumer slice into new navigation infrastructure. Left as a deliberate scope call, reopenable on its own merits if it's ever felt as a real gap.

**Tests added:** 6 cases in `CheckPartnerDebtNotificationsUseCaseTest` — fires for a partner-authored debt with the user as borrower; silent when the user is lender not borrower; silent when self-authored (seeded); silent when already raised (dedup by prefixed slot id, not raw debt id — deliberately kept as two separate id-shaped sets to avoid the exact raw-vs-prefixed remapping bug Item 1's backlog guard hit); an edit reusing the same id stays silent via the inbox's own dedup; a multi-debt mixed scenario. Suite green throughout.

**On-device verification (emulator, Medium_Phone AVD, staging seed via Supabase MCP, testdev2/testdev3 paired couple):** 6 of 7 scenarios passed cleanly with **no bugs found and no code changes needed** — backlog guard suppresses a debt that existed before the very first sync; a genuinely new partner-authored debt raises both the inbox row (exact copy: `"testdev3 logged a new debt"` / `"You owe ₱250.75."`) and the OS push, tap opens Couple with no crash; the wrong direction (user as lender) stays silent; a self-authored debt (via the in-app Add-debt dialog) never notifies its own author, immediately and after a later sync; the Settings → Notifications "Couple" section section renders with "Partner debt alerts" default ON, correctly gates a new qualifying debt while toggled off, and resumes firing once re-enabled; the dark-mode inbox row (both unread and read states) is legible, reusing Item 6's already-fixed `NotificationCard`. The 7th scenario (Couple section hidden while unpaired, via `testdev1`) was **skipped** — the test account's password didn't authenticate, an anticipated fallback, not a code gap — but the `isPaired` wiring is the same proven `ObserveCoupleMembersUseCase().map { it != null }` pattern already exercised elsewhere in the app. All 5 seeded test debts + their 2 auto-netting payment rows were soft-deleted from staging afterward.

## Item 10 — Allow overpaying a single debt row, spreading the overflow across user-chosen debts (Partner Debt Tracker)

- **Status:** GRILLED + design-locked 2026-07-25 ([ADR-0055](../adr/0055-debt-overpay-cascade-guided-allocation.md)), not yet built. **Model: Opus, high effort** — the app's **first true atomic multi-row write**, a new one-screen allocation UI, and pure money-math that is tier-1-test-required per CLAUDE.md. **No schema/Room change** (the schema question reversed at grill).
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-25):** today, settling a single debt row blocks any payment larger than that row's remaining amount. Alvin wants to **allow overpayment**, letting the excess spill across his other debts, capped at what the couple actually owes.
- **Current behavior (confirmed by inspection):** the overpayment block is a **UI-layer guard, not a domain rule** — `PartnerDebtViewModel.saveSettle()` rejects `amount > editor.remaining` ([PartnerDebtViewModel.kt:193](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/partnerdebt/presentation/PartnerDebtViewModel.kt#L193)). The domain use case underneath already tolerates overpayment — [RecordDebtPaymentUseCase.kt:14-17](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/partnerdebt/domain/usecase/RecordDebtPaymentUseCase.kt#L14-L17)'s doc comment says *"Overpayment is not an error here (the calculator floors remaining at zero) — the UI guards against it for UX."*

### Grill outcome (2026-07-25) — full design resolved, [ADR-0055](../adr/0055-debt-overpay-cascade-guided-allocation.md)

**The reframe that reshaped the feature:** auto-netting (ADR-0019) already FIFO-offsets *opposing* debts to zero at creation time, so by settlement the debts with `remaining > 0` are — normally — all in one direction and sum to exactly the couple's net. So the feature isn't a mechanical "cascade past 100%"; it's **"distribute one lump payment across my same-direction debts, capped at what I owe."** And since each debt floors at zero and the net is unchanged regardless of which debt absorbs what, the money-math end-state is identical no matter how the lump spreads — **the user's picking only controls which labeled debt gets marked paid off** (record-keeping, not math).

| Decision | Resolution |
|---|---|
| **Direction / ceiling** | Overflow flows **only** to debts where the user is the borrower ("I owe") — never into an opposing "they owe me" debt (would flip who owes whom). "Capped at net" is automatic: same-direction remainings already sum to the net (opposing are netted to zero). |
| **Why pick** | End-state is identical regardless of allocation; picking only chooses **which labeled debt gets marked paid**. Record-keeping, not money-math. |
| **UI** | **One screen, progressive disclosure.** Tap a debt, pay normally — unchanged. Only when the typed amount exceeds that debt's remaining do the other "I owe" debts appear (**unticked**). |
| **Control** | **Tick to include**, and **money fills in tick order** (first ticked = paid first, each floored at its remaining, last-touched takes the remainder). Tick order is what lets the user choose which debt is left open. Rejected: always-oldest-first fill, per-debt amount typing, drag-to-reorder, step-by-step chain dialog. |
| **Ceiling** | = **sum of the ticked debts' remaining**, live-updating as more are ticked (tapped debt always ticked). Over the ceiling ⇒ **blocked** with a clear message, never silently capped, never overshoots. Optional "Pay full ₱N" shortcut. |
| **Money (payor)** | **One** `isSettlement` EXPENSE for the whole lump (one real money movement), linked to every generated `DebtPayment` via the existing `payorTxnId`. Rejected: one expense per leg (Records clutter, untruthful). |
| **Money (receiver)** | **One** INCOME for the lump via the receiver's existing optional affordance, grouped by the shared `payorTxnId`, stamping `receiverTxnId` on all grouped payments at once. Receiver leg stays optional. |
| **Atomicity** | **All-or-nothing** — the EXPENSE + all payment rows commit in one `RoomDatabase.withTransaction` (the app's **first true atomic multi-row write**). A partial write would leave the ledger overstating what reached the debts. Deliberate departure from `SettleDebtUseCase`/`ApplyDebtNettingUseCase`'s best-effort sequential pattern (safe there because each write stands alone; not safe here — one expense backs N payments). |
| **Netting coexistence** | Auto-netting (create-time, FIFO, `isNetting=true`) and the cascade (settle-time, user-driven, ordinary `isNetting=false` payments) stay **separate paths**. The cascade only *reads* each debt's already-netted `remaining`; never runs netting. Must not be conflated in code or UI. |
| **Couples / schema** | Either partner records it unilaterally, syncs to both — no new approval. **No schema, no Room bump** (grouping rides `payorTxnId`; atomicity just wraps existing writes). ADR-0009 order unaffected. |
| **Tests** | The allocation is a **pure, tier-1-tested function** (ticked debts in tick order + lump → per-debt split): fill-in-tick-order, floor-each-at-remaining, last-debt-takes-remainder, exact-to-ceiling, over-ceiling block. |

**Build shape:** a pure `allocateOverpayment(orderedTickedDebts, lump)` function (tier-1 tests) → a new atomic use case (`SettleDebtsUseCase` or an extension) that writes the single EXPENSE + N `DebtPayment` rows inside `RoomDatabase.withTransaction` → expand `SettleDialog`/`PartnerDebtViewModel` to reveal the tickable same-direction debt list on overpay, with the live ticked-total ceiling → the receiver-side one-tap grouped income (query payments by shared `payorTxnId`).

## Item 11 — Occasional in-app nudge to try the home-screen widgets

- **Status:** PLANNED — booked 2026-07-27. **Model: Sonnet, low effort** — a direct pattern-follow of the existing dismissible-nudge-card mechanism ([PairingNudgeCard](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/analysis/presentation/AnalysisScreen.kt#L423), backed by `OnboardingRepository`'s `pairing_card_dismissed` flag) plus the already-established widget-instance query in [Widgets.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/widget/presentation/Widgets.kt#L16) (`GlanceAppWidgetManager.getGlanceIds`). No cross-ADR interaction, no sync/couple state — no grill needed. No schema/Room change.
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-27):** an occasional reminder nudging users toward the balance/quick-add home-screen widgets, since they're easy to miss and genuinely help. Scoped via clarifying questions: **only shown to non-adopters** (users who haven't placed either widget), **in-app tip card only** (no OS push, no [Item 6](#item-6--notification-bell--in-app-inbox-facility) inbox row — this is a discovery tip, not an event notification), **monthly cadence** (re-surfaces roughly every 30 days if still not adopted).
- **Detection:** new `CheckWidgetAdoptionUseCase` ([feature/widget/domain/usecase/](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/widget/), new `domain` subfolder — the widget feature currently has none) wraps `GlanceAppWidgetManager(context).getGlanceIds(BalanceWidget::class.java)` + `getGlanceIds(AddTransactionWidget::class.java)`; adopted = either list non-empty.
- **Persistence:** one new local DataStore `Long` preference, `widget_nudge_last_shown_at` (epoch millis), added to [OnboardingRepository](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/onboarding/domain/repository/OnboardingRepository.kt) / [OnboardingRepositoryImpl](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/onboarding/data/OnboardingRepositoryImpl.kt#L38) — same home as `pairing_card_dismissed`. `observeShowWidgetNudge(): Flow<Boolean>` combines the adoption check with the timestamp: visible when **not adopted AND (never shown OR ≥30 days since `last_shown_at`)**. The card's own composition (not a separate dismiss action) is what calls `recordWidgetNudgeShown()` and stamps `now()` — the ✕ button just hides it early; there's no separate "don't show again," since the 30-day gate already makes it non-naggy. Mirrors the "fire-once-per-window" shape of [Item 1](#item-1--recurring-due-date-reminder-notification-un-deferred-from-deferredmd-item-40)'s `RecurringReminderStore`, using calendar days instead of an occurrence id.
- **UI:** new `WidgetNudgeCard` composable on [TransactionsScreen.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsScreen.kt) (Records — the app's landing tab), copying `PairingNudgeCard`'s exact shape/style (`PlayfulCard`, Blush surface, title + body + ✕ `IconButton`). Draft copy: *"Try the Love, Ipon widget"* / *"Check your balance or log an expense right from your home screen."* Tapping the card body deep-links to the OS's `AppWidgetManager.requestPinAppWidget` flow where supported, else opens a short how-to (exact tap behavior confirmed at build time — not a design blocker).
- **Wiring:** `TransactionsViewModel`'s main `combine()` is already at Kotlin's 5-flow ceiling ([TransactionsViewModel.kt:91-143](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsViewModel.kt#L91-L143)) — follow the same escape hatch already used twice there (`deepHistoryLocked`, `observePrivacyMode()`, [lines 143-157](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsViewModel.kt#L143-L157)): add one more trailing `.combine(showWidgetNudgeCard) { state, show -> state.copy(showWidgetNudgeCard = show) }`. Do **not** try to widen the 5-arg combine.
- **Verify:** `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green. **Tier-1 test:** extract the "should show" decision (adopted flag + last-shown timestamp + now → visible boolean) as a pure function and unit-test the 30-day boundary; the `GlanceAppWidgetManager` query itself is thin Android-API plumbing, not unit-tested (matches `Widgets.kt`'s existing un-tested calls). On-device: fresh account with no widgets placed → open Records → card appears; add either widget to the home screen → reopen Records → card gone; dismiss the card → confirm it doesn't reappear same day; back-date `widget_nudge_last_shown_at` via `sqlite3`/prefs edit to simulate 30+ days elapsed while still not adopted → confirm it resurfaces.

## Item 12 — Opt-in off-app delivery for the recurring due-date reminder ([Item 1](#item-1--recurring-due-date-reminder-notification-un-deferred-from-deferredmd-item-40) / [ADR-0052](../adr/0052-recurring-due-date-reminder-foreground.md))

- **Status:** PLANNED — booked 2026-07-27, **not yet grilled**. Model/effort TBD at grill time — likely Sonnet/medium if it stays a pattern-follow (new `PeriodicWorkRequest` or `AlarmManager` path reusing the existing `CheckRecurringDueUseCase`/`RecurringReminderStore`), but touches ADR-0012's foreground-only posture and the Transsion/MTK force-stop caveat, so confirm at grill.
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-27):** while confirming the recurring reminder only fires on app-open/sync (by design, ADR-0052), Alvin asked for an **opt-in** option so it can also fire without opening the app — with the **current foreground/sync-triggered behavior staying the default**.
- **Why now:** ADR-0052's own Consequences section anticipated this exact ask: *"If tester feedback shows off-app reach is genuinely missed, a real alarm can be added later as its own grilled item, born aware of the force-stop-ROM caveat above."*
- **Open questions for the grill:** mechanism (`PeriodicWorkRequest` vs `AlarmManager.setAndAllowWhileIdle` vs exact alarm — the last is Play-policy-restricted on targetSdk 36); whether the force-stop-ROM caveat (a force-stopped app gets neither alarms nor WorkManager jobs, per ADR-0052) changes in weight now that it's opt-in rather than default; where the toggle lives on the Notifications screen and how it's worded given it may silently do nothing on hostile OEMs; whether it reuses `CheckRecurringDueUseCase`/`RecurringReminderStore` as-is or needs its own path; defensible cadence/battery cost; whether this amends ADR-0052 or is a new ADR.
- **Not started:** no design decisions made yet — this stub only records the ask.
